title: 2017 AMC 10B Problem 19
statement:
Let \(ABC\) be an equilateral triangle. Extend side \(\overline{AB}\) beyond \(B\) to a point \(B'\) so that \(BB'=3 \cdot AB.\) Similarly, extend side \(\overline{BC}\) beyond \(C\) to a point \(C'\) so that \(CC'=3 \cdot BC,\) and extend side \(\overline{CA}\) beyond \(A\) to a point \(A'\) so that \(AA'=3 \cdot CA.\)

What is the ratio of the area of \(\triangle A'B'C'\) to the area of \(\triangle ABC?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(X\) be the area of \(\triangle ABC.\) Each of \(\triangle BB'C,\) \(\triangle CC'A,\) and \(\triangle AA'B\) has a base three times as long as a side of \(\triangle ABC\) and the same corresponding altitude. Each therefore has area \(3X.\)

Next, \(\triangle AA'C'\) has three times the base and the same altitude as \(\triangle ACC',\) whose area is \(3X.\) Thus \(\triangle AA'C'\) has area \(9X.\) Similarly, \(\triangle CC'B'\) and \(\triangle BB'A'\) each have area \(9X.\)

These seven regions partition the large triangle, so \[\begin{aligned}[A'B'C']&=X+3(3X)+3(9X)\\&=37X.\end{aligned}\] The requested ratio is \(37:1.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E .
hints: Break the large triangle into the original triangle and six surrounding triangles
Compare each surrounding triangle area to the original using base and height
